curriculum.lesson_evidence: Sleep gives the body and brain time to repair, grow and learn. The Australian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines recommend about 9 to 11 hours of good-quality sleep for children aged 5 to 13. Good sleep habits include a regular bedtime and wake-up time, a calm routine, a dark, quiet room and no screens for the hour before bed. Not enough sleep can make us grumpy, forgetful and tired.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Maya goes to bed at 9:30 pm and wakes at 6:30 am. How many hours of sleep is that, and is it within 9 to 11 hours?

FEEDBACK
9:30 pm to 6:30 am is 9 hours. That is within 9 to 11 hours, at the lower end. A slightly earlier bedtime might help if she feels tired.

WATCH FOR
Thinking you can catch up on lost sleep whenever you like. Regular sleep each night works best for growth, mood and learning.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Plan a bedtime routine with times from dinner to wake-up. Calculate the total sleep hours and compare with 9 to 11 hours. Add three calming activities and one reason for no screens before bed. Keep a sleep diary for three nights.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: Amir's routine. Dinner at 6:00, bath at 7:00, quiet reading at 7:30, lights out at 8:00 pm, wake-up at 6:30 am. Total sleep: 10.5 hours. No tablet after 7:00. In the morning he feels alert and ready to learn.

TRY FIRST
Maya goes to bed at 9:30 pm and wakes at 6:30 am. How many hours of sleep is that, and is it within 9 to 11 hours?

FEEDBACK
9:30 pm to 6:30 am is 9 hours. That is within 9 to 11 hours, at the lower end. A slightly earlier bedtime might help if she feels tired.
teach_steps.explain:
Sleep gives the body and brain time to repair, grow and learn. The Australian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines recommend about 9 to 11 hours of good-quality sleep for children aged 5 to 13. Good sleep habits include a regular bedtime and wake-up time, a calm routine, a dark, quiet room and no screens for the hour before bed. Not enough sleep can make us grumpy, forgetful and tired.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.
